1. Whether reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see the judgment?

2.      To be referred to the Reporter or not?

 

JUSTICE J.D. KAPOOR, PRESIDENT (ORAL)   The limited grievance of the appellant against the impugned order dated 11th January 2007, passed by the District Forum, whereby the appellant has been directed to repair the Washing Machine purchased by the respondent and issue fresh warranty for two years from the date of complete repair free of charges and to pay Rs. 4,000/- as compensation and Rs. 1,000/- as cost of litigation, is against the direction to issue fresh warranty of two years.

2. Admittedly the appellant is the manufacturer of Washing Machine. Respondent purchased one Washing Machine on 1st August, 2004 for a consideration amount of Rs. 16,500/-. The machine started giving trouble. The respondent who is a senior citizen lodged several complaints but the machine could not be repaired. Finally the appellant replaced the Washing Machine on 28th January, 2006. Since the problem i.e. chin problem continued with the new machine, the appellant filed the instant complaint before the District Forum for replacing of the Washing Machine, cost and compensation.

3. According to the learned counsel for the appellant once the machine was replaced by a new machine, the appellant should not have been directed to give fresh warranty of two years as the original warranty in respect of the original machine could be treated or deemed as continued warranty. In support of this contention the learned counsel for the appellant has placed reliance upon warranty clause 6 in respect of the original machine which provides that the warranty shall not in any case extend towards payment of any monetary consideration whatsoever or replacement or return of the Product.

4. So far as the remedy to a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act is concerned, it is an independent remedy and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force. Section 14 provides that if the goods are found to be suffering from any of the defects specified in the complaint or that any of the allegations contained in the complaint about the services are proved, the District Forums/State Commission have powers to direct the trader to do one or more of the following things, namely

(i)     To remove the defect pointed out by the appropriate laboratory from the goods in question

(ii)   To replace goods with new goods of similar description which shall be free from any defect;

(iii)  To return to the complainant the price, or as the case may be, the charges paid by the complainant; and

(iv)            To pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation of the consumer for any loss or injury suffered by the consumer due to the negligence of the opposite party.

 

5. We have taken a view that wherever goods have been found defective and give constant problem irrespective of the fact that there is a manufacturing defect or not, the problem should be solved once for all. In such cases replacement of the goods with new goods of similar description which shall be free from any defect is not a practical solution. Sub-section (b) of Section 14(1) specifically provides that if trader has been directed to replace the goods with new goods of similar description, these goods have to be free from any defect and if the new goods also suffer from any defect then the trader is liable to not only compensate the consumer as to the mental agony, harassment suffered by him but also shall be liable to replace that good also with new goods.

6. The whole purpose and object of replacement of the goods with the new goods of similar description would lose its meaning and import if the trader is absolved of the liability to escape from furnishing fresh warranty. The new goods tentamount to a fresh contract. Replacement of old goods by new goods tentamounts to a fresh contract and therefore the trader has to furnish a fresh warranty in respect of the new goods. There is no escape from such a liability.

7. In our view the replacement of the goods of new goods is not the better solution as is demonstrated by the instant case.

If the new goods are found to be defective the parties are relegated to square one or the second bout of litigation which does not augur well either for the traders or for the consumer.

8. In our view the best solution to such a problem is to direct the trader to return the price of the goods or the charges paid by the complainant with a reasonable amount of compensation as to the mental agony and harassment suffered by the consumer which includes physical discomfort, emotional sufferings and the injustice done to him.

9. In the result, we modify the impugned order by allowing the appeal partly with the direction to the appellant to refund the cost of the machine i.e. Rs. 16,500/- with the compensation of Rs. 4,000/- and Rs. 1,000/- as cost of litigation awarded by the district Forum and set aside the rest of the order. This will be an end to the ongoing feud and dispute between the parties over a goods which is used everyday and occurrence of the problem every day causes immense inconvenience to the consumer.

10. Appeal is modified to the aforesaid extent.

11. F.D.R./Bank Guarantee, if any, furnished by the appellant be returned forthwith after completion of due formalities.

12. A copy of this order as per the statutory requirements, be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to Record Room.

13. Announced on the 13th April, 2007.

   

(Justice J.D. Kapoor) President     (Rumnita Mittal) Member jj
